name: same-character-v2
summary: Asks a vision model whether a full-body edit shows the same character as its design, body plan included (heads, arms, legs, tails, wings), and which props changed.

steps.name: compare
steps.prompt: You compare two pencil drawings for a game tool. Image 1 (the first image) is a character design. Image 2 (the second image) is meant to redraw the same character as a full-body, front-facing A-pose. These differences are expected and are not changes: the pose, camera angle, framing and how much of the body is visible; lines, shading and paper; parts hidden in image 1 now being drawn; and a weapon or prop that was held in a hand now worn on the back or belt. Decide whether image 2 shows the same character as image 1: the same kind of person or creature, the same face and hair or headgear, the same costume and armour pieces, and the same body: as many heads, arms, legs, tails and wings as image 1 shows or clearly implies (parts that the framing of image 1 cuts off count as present when the kind of body implies them). List every head, arm, leg, tail or wing that image 2 adds or drops as a body change; a character with a body change is not the same character. Then list the weapons and carried props you can see in each image (swords, guns, staffs, shields, bags, and so on; not clothing). A prop is added when image 2 has it and image 1 shows no such prop at all; removed when image 1 has it and image 2 shows it nowhere, worn or held. Judge only what you see. Reply with JSON only.
